title: What If a City's River Became an Open Sewer? London's Great Stink

scenes.text: What if a capital city's river turned into an open sewer? London's Parliament had to run.
In the hot summer of 1858, the Thames dropped low, and the sewage along its banks baked in the heat.
The smell was so bad that MPs doused the Parliament curtains in chloride of lime.
Lime and carbolic acid were poured into the river, and it did not help.
Lawmakers passed a bill for a new sewer in just eighteen days, a record.
Engineer Joseph Bazalgette built brick tunnels and pumping stations, finished in 1875. A smell fixed the city's drains.
